title: Ramayana Becomes First Bollywood Film to Cross Rs 50 Crore in Kerala
excerpt: Trade trackers estimate the Hindi epic passed Rs 50 crore gross in Kerala in its second week, nearly 160% above the previous Bollywood record, and the milestone makes Yash the first actor to open the state's 50-crore club for two industries.
body:
• Ramayana: Part 1 has crossed Rs 50 crore gross in Kerala, becoming the first Bollywood film ever to reach that mark in the state, according to trade tracker Pinkvilla's estimates.
  • The previous Bollywood record in Kerala was Dhurandhar 2's lifetime gross of Rs 19.25 crore, according to Koimoi — no Hindi film had previously crossed even Rs 20 crore in the state.
  • Yash, who plays Ravana, is now the only actor to have headlined the first Rs 50 crore Kerala grosser for two different industries: Kannada cinema with KGF: Chapter 2 in 2022, and Bollywood with Ramayana, according to Koimoi.
  • The Hindi-language epic, directed by Nitesh Tiwari and starring Ranbir Kapoor as Ram and Sai Pallavi alongside Yash, reached the milestone on its second Monday, in its 12th day in theatres.

Kerala has long been the hardest southern market for Hindi cinema to crack. Ramayana: Part 1 has now done what no Bollywood film managed before it: trade tracker Pinkvilla estimates the film's Kerala gross has crossed Rs 50 crore, collected in 12 days, making it the first Bollywood release ever to enter the state's Rs 50 crore club. Box office figures in India are trade estimates compiled by trackers, not certified studio accounts, and the trackers' day counts differ slightly — Koimoi reported the film storming past the milestone in its 13th day — but both trackers agree on the crossing and on what it displaces.

"Koimoi credited a Rs 17.50 crore second weekend and steady weekday holds across Malayalam-language and 3D screenings."

A record that was not close

Before Ramayana, the Bollywood ceiling in Kerala stood below Rs 20 crore. Ranveer Singh's Dhurandhar 2 held the all-time Bollywood record in the state with a lifetime gross of Rs 19.25 crore, according to Koimoi, which put Ramayana's Kerala gross at nearly 160% above that benchmark and still counting. Pinkvilla's day-wise estimates show how the film got there: a Rs 6.25 crore tenth day, Rs 6.75 crore on day 11, and Rs 3.75 to 4 crore on its second Monday — a drop of only 15% from the previous Friday — to reach Rs 50 crore. Koimoi credited a Rs 17.50 crore second weekend and steady weekday holds across Malayalam-language and 3D screenings.

Why Yash is the story inside the story

The film stars Ranbir Kapoor as Ram and Sai Pallavi, with Yash as Ravana. For Yash, the Kerala milestone is a repeat in a different industry's colours. He first broke the state's Rs 50 crore barrier in 2022 with Prashanth Neel's KGF: Chapter 2, the first Kannada film to cross that mark in Kerala, according to Koimoi. With Ramayana, Koimoi noted, he becomes the only actor in India to have headlined the very first Rs 50 crore-plus Kerala grosser for two different film industries.

Ramayana now completes Koimoi's list of the films that first unlocked Kerala's Rs 50 crore club for their industries: Pulimurugan for Malayalam cinema, Jailer for Tamil, Baahubali 2 for Telugu, KGF: Chapter 2 for Kannada, and now Ramayana for Bollywood.

What the film is, and what comes next

Ramayana: Part 1 is a Hindi-language epic directed by Nitesh Tiwari, retelling the Ramayana with Ranbir Kapoor as Ram and Yash as Ravana; in Kerala it is playing in Malayalam-language and 3D screenings as well as Hindi. The film is in theatres now, in India and in overseas markets where it released with the Indian run.

Both trackers expect the Kerala run to keep going. Koimoi put the film as eyeing a Rs 75 crore-plus lifetime gross in the state, and Pinkvilla said a Rs 75 crore finish is within reach if the momentum holds after the release of Dhanush and Mammootty's O.M Chapter 1, with Rs 100 crore an outside possibility. Those are tracker projections, not results — but a Bollywood film being projected at those numbers in Kerala is itself the news.
